pressure.title: Upflow velocity sets the cut size
pressure.description: Coarse hydrate crystals settle faster than the rising liquor and report to the underflow as product (to filtration and calcination). Fine crystals are carried up with the overflow and returned to precipitation as seed. The cut size is set by the overflow rate per unit area (upflow velocity) and slurry density — the key to controlling product particle size.

foundation: Large ring foundation or concrete tank; centre pier carries the rake drive and torque.
alignment: Level launders so overflow is even all round; centre the drive and shaft.
piping: Feed to feedwell with flocculant dosing points; underflow pumps with standby and flushing; overflow to downstream.
commissioning: Fill with water, run rakes and test torque alarms and lift; start feed and flocculant; build mud bed gradually.

lubrication: Agitator gearbox oil and motor bearings per maker; no lubrication for static parts.

video_tutorials.title: Seed Classification Unit — Introduction

script.narration: This module introduces the Seed Classification Unit.
A seed classification unit splits precipitated hydrate by size.
In a gravity classifier, coarse crystals settle against the rising liquor and leave in the underflow as product; fine crystals are carried up with the overflow and returned as seed.
Typical applications include product/seed split in precipitation circuits; fine-seed recovery for agglomeration; control of product particle size.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Underflow Pump (coarse hydrate → product), Underflow Pump (coarse hydrate → product) — Shaft & Coupling (turning).
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: How the Seed Classification Unit works.
Hydrate slurry enters the feedwell.
Coarse crystals settle to the cone.
Fines rise to the overflow launder.
The underflow pump takes product.
The flow overlay traces the liquid from suction to discharge.
Coarse hydrate crystals settle faster than the rising liquor and report to the underflow as product (to filtration and calcination).

video_tutorials.title: Seed Classification Unit — Maintenance

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Seed Classification Unit.
Check underflow density and size.
Clear scale in cone.
Pump overhaul.
Watch for wrong cut: product too fine/coarse. Common cause: flow or density change.
Watch for cone blockage: no underflow. Common cause: scale, coarse build-up.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
